title: Social cohesion is becoming an operational development mechanism measured through bonding, bridging and linking relations rather than a single community score
source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 10417, Leveraging Social Cohesion for Development Outcomes
geography: Global development and fragile, conflict and violence-affected contexts, with evidence and examples spanning multiple regions

observations.period: 2023 working paper; social-cohesion measurement and development practice

denominator.unit: relational dimensions of social cohesion defined by the paper

bonding.value: relations connecting people within a community

bridging.value: relations connecting members of distinct communities or groups

linking.value: relations connecting people and communities to institutions or actors with power

observations.method: World Bank policy research paper that reviews definitions, measurement strategies and evidence on interventions intended to strengthen social cohesion.
observations.uncertainty: The framework separates relational dimensions but does not imply that one index can capture all forms of trust, cooperation, identity, power or conflict dynamics.
observations.subgroup: Individuals within communities, groups divided across identity or status lines, citizens, public institutions, local leaders, civil society and development actors.
observations.counterinterpretation: Bonding within a group can support mutual aid while reinforcing exclusion or hostility toward outsiders; bridging and linking relations can also be unequal or coercive.

observations.period: 2023 working paper; diagnosis and measurement strategy

diagnosis.value: the three relational dimensions provide a framework for diagnosing gaps in cohesion

tracking.value: the paper recommends tracking trends separately across bonding, bridging and linking rather than assuming cohesion is one condition

investment.value: the framework is intended to help prioritize interventions and development investments

observations.method: Conceptual and evidence review with recommendations for teams designing social-cohesion measurement strategies.
observations.uncertainty: Measurement choices remain context-dependent; the paper does not provide a globally harmonized time series or a single threshold for healthy cohesion.
observations.subgroup: Development teams, governments, researchers, civil-society organizations, community groups and populations affected by fragility or displacement.
observations.counterinterpretation: More detailed measurement can improve targeting but can also fragment the construct, over-quantify relationships or expose communities without delivering resources or remedy.

within_group.value: some interventions can reinforce cohesion within communities

across_group.value: some interventions can build trust across groups

citizen_state.value: some interventions can strengthen relations between citizens and the state

observations.method: Review of evidence on different intervention types intended to repair or reinforce social cohesion, including community, intergroup and citizen-state pathways.
observations.uncertainty: The paper emphasizes contradictory evidence and states that effectiveness depends on sound diagnosis and rigorous implementation; it is not a universal intervention ranking.
observations.subgroup: Residents of divided or fragile communities, public-service users, local organizations, state institutions and development-program participants.
observations.counterinterpretation: An intervention can improve one relational dimension while worsening another—for example, strengthening internal solidarity without improving cross-group trust or institutional accountability.

observations.period: 2023 working paper; development and fragility application

operational_route.value: social cohesion is presented as a mechanism through which development projects can affect trust, cooperation, collective action and development outcomes

implementation_condition.value: intervention effectiveness is conditional on accurate diagnosis and rigorous implementation processes

scope.value: the framework is relevant to fragile communities and development projects but must be tailored to local context

observations.method: Policy research synthesis connecting social-cohesion concepts and evidence to development operations and measurement practice.
observations.uncertainty: The working paper is not a project-level impact evaluation and does not show that applying the framework produces durable peace, service quality or poverty reduction.
observations.subgroup: Communities affected by fragility, conflict and violence, displaced and host populations, local governments, development practitioners and service-delivery institutions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Social-cohesion programming can complement material investment, but it cannot substitute for security, rights, public services, economic opportunity or accountable institutions.

related_sources.claim: Official World Bank PDF for Policy Research Working Paper 10417, April 2023.
World Bank social-cohesion and resilience program context linking social cohesion to fragility, conflict, displacement and development operations.

boundary: This record adds a social-cohesion measurement and intervention route linking bonding, bridging and linking relations to trust, identity, participation, citizen-state relations, development investment and conflict or fragility outcomes. It is a 2023 World Bank working-paper synthesis, not a current global prevalence estimate, respondent-level dataset, single intervention evaluation, U.S.-specific result or proof that social-cohesion programming produces durable peace or shared prosperity.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official World Bank working-paper PDF and World Bank social-cohesion program page were reviewed for the bonding, bridging and linking framework, measurement recommendations, intervention evidence and context-dependent implementation limits.
